One-line judgment: this line of work is neither pressing a button to machine nor casually writing code, but developing programs that control automatic machine tools or machining systems, turning drawings and process requirements into tool paths and numerical control code and validating them through simulation and trial cutting, and possibly being responsible for fixturing and operating and maintaining equipment. O*NET defines the occupation as developing programs to control automatic machine tools, equipment or systems to machine or process materials; may also be responsible for setting up, operating or maintaining equipment; its tasks are led by determining the sequence of machining operations and selecting the appropriate tools needed to machine the workpiece into the target shape and analyzing work orders and drawings and specifications and design data to calculate dimensions and tool selection and machine speeds and feeds, and this page is developed on the precise occupational scope of O*NET-SOC 51-9162.00, for which the occupational page marks Bright Outlook.

Signals for continuing to explore: you are willing to do process reasoning from the constraints of drawings and tolerances and materials and machines and fixtures, write tool paths and parameters into a verifiable program, and accept the repeated iteration of simulate first, then trial cut, then measure the first article. O*NET work context shows 88% wear common protective or safety equipment every day (12% once a week or more), 56% have face-to-face discussions every day (42% once a week or more), 60% continuously or almost continuously use hands to handle objects and tools (33% more than half the time), 64% consider being very exact or highly accurate extremely important (14% very important, 22% important), 41% make decisions every day that affect others or financial resources or organizational reputation (45% once a week or more), 41% face strict deadlines every day (38% once a week or more), 50% consider their decisions very important to company results (22% important), 51% have a lot of freedom in determining tasks and priorities and goals (24% some freedom), 47% consider repetitive tasks extremely important (15% very important, 26% important), 40% have a lot of decision freedom (34% some freedom), 47% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day, 39% are exposed to hazardous equipment every day (35% never), and 78% work 40 hours per week (22% more than 40 hours).

Conditions for pausing before high investment: you have not yet gone through a complete loop of reading drawings and process analysis — tool and operation selection — tool path and parameter writing — simulation and single block validation — trial cut and first-article measurement — iterating from dimensional and surface results, in a simulation or paper process, nor have you checked the employer rules on program release, post-processing and machine controller matching, simulation and trial cutting, and lockout/tagout and guarding. The preparation level for this occupation is Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation needed), the education distribution wording on that page is that a high school diploma or equivalent is usually required and some positions do not require it, and the SVP range is less than 6.0; that page also lists 7 registered apprenticeship role examples (Cnc Operator and Programmer, Cnc Set-Up Prog - Milling, Cnc Set-Up Programmer Milling and Turning, Tool Programmer, Numerical and others), but apprenticeship experience and training do not equal program release authority, and this page does not infer an individual hiring probability from them.

Education, job training, professional certification, licenses and position authority must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation needed), the education distribution wording on that page is that a high school diploma or equivalent is usually required and some positions do not require it, and the SVP range is less than 6.0; that page also lists 7 registered apprenticeship role examples and provides 1 national certification entry; but apprenticeship experience and certification do not equal a degree, an employer appointment, program release or machine tool operating authorization; program release and post-processing configuration, simulation and trial cutting requirements, and hazardous energy control (lockout/tagout) and machine guarding requirements before maintenance and troubleshooting must be confirmed item by item against the applicable jurisdiction and employer systems; this page explains tasks and boundaries based on O*NET and public sources and does not present education or certification as a statutory qualification.

One line: this is an occupation in which calculating correctly, writing it out and validating it are all indispensable; whether the tool path is right, whether the parameters hold up, and whether simulation and trial cutting can find the problems determine whether your program is released to the machine. If you are willing to speak with geometry and tolerances and trials rather than trial-and-error counts, it deserves serious consideration.

The work of numerically controlled machine tool programmers can be divided into three linked but independent work dimensions. The first is drawing reading and process planning: analyze work orders and drawings and blueprints and specifications and printed circuit board artwork films and design data to calculate dimensions and tool selection and machine speeds and feeds; determine the sequence of machining operations and select the appropriate tools needed to machine the workpiece into the target shape; determine datum points and machine cutting paths or hole positions and calculate angles and linear dimensions and radii and curvatures; group shop work orders to improve material utilization and reduce setup time; prepare geometric layouts from graphic displays using computer-aided drafting software or drafting tools and graph paper; and order tooling for workpieces. The second is program writing and simulation validation: write programs in the machine controller language and store the programs on media such as paper tape and magnetic tape or disks; observe the machine during trial runs or perform computer simulation to ensure the program and machine run correctly and produce parts that meet specifications; modify programs or paper tape to eliminate errors and re-test to confirm the problem is resolved; modify existing programs to improve efficiency; enter hole position coordinates into program memory through a programmer's foot pedal or keys; and compare encoded paper tape or computer printouts with the original part specifications and drawings to verify that the instructions are accurate. The third is data and media and documentation and maintenance: enter computer instructions to store or retrieve part graphics and graphic displays or programs and transfer data to other media; write instruction sheets and tool lists for machine controllers to guide setup and encode numerical control paper tape; align and secure template film on the reference table of an optical programmer and observe magnified views of printed circuit boards; and perform preventive maintenance or minor repairs on machine tools.

Drawing reading and process planning: analyze work orders and drawings and specifications and design data, determine operation sequence and tools, determine datum and tool paths and hole positions and calculate dimensions and radii and curvatures, group work orders and order tooling

Read drawings and specifications → set operations and tools and datum → calculate tool paths and dimensions and parameters → write or modify the program → simulation and single block validation → trial cut the first article and compare with specifications and archive records

Program writing and simulation validation: write programs in the controller language, validate in trial runs or simulation, modify programs for errors and re-test, optimize existing programs, enter coordinates and compare instructions with drawings

Set operations and tools → generate tool paths and code → simulate to check collision and overcut → single block dry run → trial cut and measure the first article → correct deviations and keep version records

Data and media and documentation and maintenance: store and retrieve and transfer part graphics and programs, write instruction sheets and tool lists, align template film and observe magnified views, and perform preventive maintenance or minor repairs on machine tools.

Program development and process validation are the focus of this occupation, and fixturing / operation / maintenance are allowed. CNC operators may also modify / write simple programs; adjacent software / hardware / electromechanical / robotics / drafting duties may overlap, and the specific final responsibility is checked against the organization. The adjacent China occupation multi-process CNC machine tool operator and adjuster 6-18-01-07 (2021 standard) is defined as operating CNC machining lines / combined / composite machine tools / machining centers to cut, including tasks such as program verification and automatic programming; it is not equivalent to the U.S. programmer statistical occupation and no corresponding wage can be inferred.

Make the machine produce conforming parts according to the program: turn drawings and process requirements into a runnable program, and hold dimensions and surface quality in simulation and trial cutting

Develop and validate numerical control programs: analyze drawings and specifications, determine operations and tools and tool paths and parameters, write and modify programs, simulate and trial cut and identify efficiency improvements

Advance the work based on the O*NET occupational definition and 16 tasks, drawings and process documents and design data, machine and controller and post-processing and tool and fixture and material conditions, and the employer systems for program release and simulation and trial cutting and safety

This occupation emphasizes program development and validation, while CNC operators emphasize operation but may also rewrite simple programs; they are distinguished by actual job duties and are not mutually exclusive.

Editorial cycle example: read the drawing → set operations / tools / datum → program → simulate / trial run per the machine model approved procedure → measure → iterate and archive, without substituting for the safety or release procedure.

Editorial six judgments: whether drawings are read to a calculable level, whether operations / tools / datum have a process basis, whether code / post-processing match, whether validation follows the machine model, whether measurement iterates, and whether versions are traceable. The specific organizational procedures are checked separately.
Judgment one: whether drawings and specifications and design data are read to a calculable level

Turn drawing dimensions and tolerances and surface requirements and material and heat treatment state and work order requirements into calculable inputs (datum and key dimensions and fits and geometric tolerances); confirm ambiguities or missing items with design and process staff before programming; do not substitute unfounded practices such as modifying an old program for verification.
Judgment two: whether operation and tool and datum selection has a process basis

Arrange roughing and finishing sequence and the number of setups according to material and structural stiffness and precision requirements; select tools and tool holders according to structural features and calculate overhang and rigidity; clarify the datum and alignment method and explain the effect on the dimension chain.
Judgment three: whether tool paths and parameters and post-processing match the machine and controller

Check tool paths and code and post-processing against machine travel and spindle and tool magazine and fixtures and controller model; confirm that feed and speed and depth of cut are within the allowable range for the tool and material; confirm coordinate systems and tool tip follow settings for multi-axis and composite operations.
Judgment four: whether simulation and single block validation cover collision and overcut and interference

Editorial suggestion: trained authorized personnel follow validation procedures approved for the machine model / process to check for collision / overcut and so on, recording problems and making revisions; simulation and single block dry running do not guarantee that all risks are ruled out, and the fictional exercise does not start a real machine.
Judgment five: whether the first article is measured and iterated against specifications

After trial cutting, measure key dimensions and geometric characteristics with precision gauges and judge against specifications; analyze the cause of out-of-tolerance (tool offset and tool wear and thermal deformation and fixturing and program errors) before correcting; record the parameters and results before and after correction and give a conclusion on whether release is possible.
Judgment six: whether programs and validation and deviation corrections are versioned and traceable

Keep programs and post-processing and tool tables and parameters and simulation and trial cutting and deviation correction and release records; specify version and modifier and time and reason; let the operators and programmers taking over restore the current machining state from the records.

The six directions share some capabilities with this occupation: reading drawings and tolerances, modeling and calculating with software, validating and recording according to procedures, and communicating with operations and process and quality staff. The real difference lies in the scope of responsibility: this occupation focuses on turning drawings and process requirements into a runnable and validated numerical control program; the operator direction focuses on execution and self-inspection; the general software direction focuses on software and systems; the hardware direction focuses on hardware design and validation; the mechatronics direction focuses on cross-disciplinary system integration and design; the robotics direction focuses on robotic systems and motion control solutions; the drafting direction focuses on drawing and documentation expression. When choosing, it is suggested to first verify with a deliverable exercise of reading drawings — setting operations and tools — generating tool paths — simulation and first-article validation, rather than comparing titles first.

The comparison is based on the occupational definition and 16 tasks and work activities and work context descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 51-9162.00 page, the related and adjacent occupation codes listed there, the adjacent occupation slug list registered in this evidence route (computer-programmers, computer-hardware-engineers, mechatronics-engineers, robotics-engineers, mechanical-drafters), and public occupational materials for each adjacent occupation; this evidence route also registers the scope difference of the adjacent Mainland China occupation multi-process CNC machine tool operator and adjuster (6-18-01-07); the comparison is editorial synthesis and does not constitute an occupational safety, quality or legal conclusion.

The table below compares roles and occupations adjacent to this occupation: numerically controlled machine tool operators, computer programmers, computer hardware engineers, mechatronics engineers, robotics engineers, and mechanical drafters. The four columns each answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Numerically controlled machine tool operators focus on executing machining according to an established program and self-inspecting, and usually do not carry development responsibility for tool paths and parameters and post-processing; this occupation takes program development and process validation as its object.
People willing to do machining execution and first-article self-inspection suit that direction; people willing to do process reasoning and program validation suit this occupation.
Mainly fixturing and first-article and patrol inspection and equipment records.
Numerically controlled machine tool operators

Computer programmers focus on program development and maintenance for general software and systems and usually do not involve machine tool and tool and material constraints; this occupation takes numerical control programs and cutting processes as its object.
People willing to do general software development suit that direction; people willing to do manufacturing processes and CNC programming suit this occupation.
Mainly software and system code and test records.
Computer programmers

Computer hardware engineers focus on hardware design and validation and usually do not carry part machining processes and program development; this occupation takes machining processes and code as its object.
People willing to do hardware design and validation suit that direction; people willing to do manufacturing processes and program development suit this occupation.
Mainly hardware design and validation and test records.
Computer hardware engineers

Mechatronics engineers focus on the system integration and design of mechanical and electrical and control systems and usually do not carry program development for a single machine tool; this occupation takes machine tool programs and process validation as its object.
People willing to do cross-disciplinary system integration and design suit that direction; people willing to do single-machine programs and process optimization suit this occupation.
Mainly system design and integration and commissioning records.
Mechatronics engineers

Robotics engineers focus on robotic system and motion control solution design and usually do not carry cutting processes and numerical control code development; this occupation takes cutting processes and numerical control programs as its object.
People willing to do robotics and motion control solutions suit that direction; people willing to do cutting processes and program validation suit this occupation.
Mainly robotics solutions and simulation and control records.
Robotics engineers

Mechanical drafters focus on the expression and conversion of drawings and technical documentation and usually do not carry process parameters and tool paths and program development; this occupation turns drawings into a runnable machining program.
People willing to do drafting and technical documentation suit that direction; people willing to do process calculation and code generation suit this occupation.
Mainly drawing and technical documentation records.
Mechanical drafters

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually requires adding new capabilities and experience: the operator direction needs on-site fixturing and first-article self-inspection and equipment maintenance experience; the general software direction needs data structures and engineering development experience; the hardware direction needs circuit and structural and validation experience; the mechatronics direction needs mechanical and electrical and control integration experience; the robotics direction needs kinematics and trajectory and control solution experience; the drafting direction needs drafting standards and documentation expression experience. Drawing reading and tolerances and software and validation capabilities can transfer, but the scope of responsibility and authority of each direction must be re-established.

Roles that carry process and tool and datum selection
Improper operation sequence or tool selection or datum selection will cause dimensional out-of-tolerance and tool breakage and scrapped workpieces during machining, and affect delivery and cost.

Arrange roughing and finishing and the number of setups according to material and structural stiffness and precision requirements; select tools and tool holders according to structural features and calculate overhang and rigidity; clarify the datum and dimension chain effect and have process or design confirm it.
Reusing an old process without adapting to the material and machine; using tools and parameters beyond the rigidity range; changing the datum with the setup without explanation.
Roles that carry program and post-processing and simulation validation

Tool paths or parameters or post-processing that do not match the machine and controller and fixtures will cause collision and overcut and machine crashes and may damage the spindle and tools and fixtures.

The editorial suggestion is to check post-processing and tooling and fixtures / material against the validation procedure approved by machine model / process, and keep simulation and on-site results; dry running / single block does not guarantee all risks are ruled out, and on-site work is carried out by trained authorized personnel.
Skipping simulation on experience; running post-processing from another machine directly on this machine; changing code on site without reporting or leaving records.
Roles that carry first-article and iteration release
Entering batch production without measuring the first article or analyzing deviations will keep producing out-of-tolerance parts in batch machining, causing rework and scrapping and customer claims.

After trial cutting, measure key dimensions and geometric characteristics with precision gauges and judge against specifications; analyze the cause of out-of-tolerance before correcting parameters and tool paths; record the results before and after correction and give a conclusion on whether release is possible.
Only looking at appearance and not measuring dimensions for the first article; treating in-process compensation as a program correction; approving batch production without confirmation.
Roles that carry version and documentation and handover responsibility
Incomplete program versions and post-processing and tool tables and release records cannot be restored at shift change and accountability and process reuse, and cause repeated incidents.

Keep programs and post-processing and tool tables and simulation and trial cutting and deviation correction and release records; specify version and modifier and time and reason; let the operators and programmers taking over restore the current machining state from the records.
Renaming files casually; several people sharing the same version without leaving modification traces; tool tables inconsistent with programs without synchronized updates.
Roles that carry on-site safety and energy control responsibility

Failing to control hazardous energy according to the procedure (lockout/tagout) before maintenance and troubleshooting and cleaning, or inadequate guarding and personal protection, will cause personal injury and compliance liability.

Applicable U.S. machine hazard points need effective guarding, and maintenance subject to 1910.147 must be isolated and verified according to the procedure, and a stop button is not an isolation device; exceptions are conditional and are not applied on your own initiative. Specific tasks are checked against the machine model / organization and the jurisdiction.
Removing or shorting guards for easier observation; entering equipment interiors while energized or without energy release; clearing chips and changing tools with bare hands.
Roles that carry program and process data confidentiality
Leakage of drawings and processes and programs and customer part data lowers competitive barriers and creates contract and compliance and customer trust risk.

Manage access and export according to information classification and least necessity and keep records; desensitize identifiable information or use controlled systems; define clear data and access boundaries for third-party and external service connections.
Uploading drawings and programs to unauthorized tools or channels; sharing high-privilege accounts; sharing part data externally without desensitization.

entries.answer: Daily work centers on drawing reading and process planning, program writing and simulation validation, and data and media and documentation and maintenance: analyze work orders and drawings and specifications and design data to calculate dimensions and tool selection and speed and feed; determine the sequence of machining operations and select appropriate tools; determine datum points and cutting paths or hole positions and calculate dimensions and radii and curvatures; write programs in the controller language and store them on media; validate programs in trial runs or simulation and modify for errors and re-test; modify existing programs to improve efficiency; compare encoded paper tape or printouts with the original specifications and drawings; write instruction sheets and tool lists; and perform preventive maintenance or minor repairs on machine tools. The work context shown on this page: 88% wear common protective or safety equipment every day, 64% consider being very exact or highly accurate extremely important, and 47% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day.
entries.question: What does a numerically controlled machine tool programmer do every day?

entries.answer: Numerically controlled machine tool operators focus on executing machining according to an established program and self-inspecting; computer programmers focus on program development and maintenance for general software and systems; computer hardware engineers focus on hardware design and validation; mechatronics engineers focus on the system integration and design of mechanical and electrical and control systems; robotics engineers focus on robotic system and motion control solution design; mechanical drafters focus on the expression and conversion of drawings and technical documentation. This occupation focuses on turning drawings and process requirements into a runnable and validated numerical control program and usually does not carry general software development or mechanical structure design responsibility. Shared capabilities do not mean the roles are interchangeable: the scope of responsibility and the authority differ. Note also that the adjacent occupational skill standard registered for Mainland China is the multi-process CNC machine tool operator and adjuster (6-18-01-07), which merges operation and adjustment with some advanced programming duties, so cross-market comparison must keep the scopes separate.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between this occupation and adjacent occupations?

entries.answer: It cannot be inferred that way. The core tasks of this occupation include operation and tool and datum selection, tool path and parameter and post-processing fit judgment, collision and overcut judgment, and release and iteration decisions; these steps depend on process experience and authority and responsibility. This evidence route also explicitly requires that AI or CAM generated tool paths and code still be simulated for the specific machine and controller and post-processor and fixtures and material and tool conditions, reviewed by authorized personnel and run safely on trial. In addition, the ILO exposure index registered in this evidence route is only a task exposure measure, not a replacement rate or job reduction forecast. The more reliable uses of tools are parameter conversion and code annotation and difference comparison and documentation drafts.
entries.question: Will AI replace numerically controlled machine tool programmers?

entries.answer: From the task structure, the earlier-affected parts are the structurable and digitizable steps: parameter conversion and code annotation and difference comparison, process and tool list organization, and measurement data aggregation and deviation classification and change record drafts. The later-affected parts are the steps requiring process judgment and responsibility: operation and datum and tool selection, post-processing fit and collision and overcut judgment, and first-article acceptability judgment and release and iteration decisions. The adjacent research directions registered in this route (adaptive machining, predictive maintenance, digital twins, AI process optimization and in-line measurement) will strengthen program preparation and validation and monitoring, but do not equal automatic replacement of the whole occupation. It must be stressed that this judgment is editorial synthesis, not an exposure measure or job forecast provided by a source.

entries.answer: Converging drawings and materials and machine constraints into a feasible operation and tool and datum plan, making trade-offs among precision and efficiency and tool life and bearing the consequences, judging whether post-processing and tool paths will cause collision and overcut on the specific machine, and completing release and first-article judgment and safety procedures per the system. These capabilities depend on process experience and authority; replacing any of these steps with tool output makes the question of who is responsible for program release and first-article acceptability unanswerable.

description.text: Numerically controlled machine tool programmers develop programs that control automatic machine tools or machining systems and validate tool paths and processes, centered on drawing reading and process planning, program writing and simulation validation, and data and media and documentation and maintenance: 16 tasks and the work context, the U.S. 2025 median wage of 68,120 USD and the employment projection registered in this route (about 28,600 → about 30,300, growth 5.9%), the two clearly labeled Mainland China manufacturing annual average wage proxies (113,594 / 76,055 yuan / year) and the occupation-level scope boundary, and entry and qualifications and release and safety boundaries and the exercise, all in one view.

subject.name: Numerically controlled machine tool programmer
subject.summary: Develop programs that control automatic machine tools or machining systems, turning drawings and process requirements into tool paths and numerical control code and validating them through simulation and trial cutting, and possibly be responsible for fixturing, operating or maintaining equipment: analyze work orders and drawings and specifications and design data to calculate dimensions and tool selection and speed and feed; determine the sequence of machining operations and select appropriate tools; determine datum points and cutting paths or hole positions and calculate dimensions and radii and curvatures; write programs in the controller language and store them on media; validate in trial runs or simulation and modify for errors and re-test; modify existing programs to improve efficiency; compare encoded output with the original specifications and drawings; write instruction sheets and tool lists; and perform preventive maintenance or minor repairs on machine tools.
